chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: The downtown halls and clubs, one for every color
summary: Danny lists Economy Hall, Cooperators Hall, Globe Hall, San Jacinto and the Lions Club, each for a different color stratum.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You had this abundance of halls! Downtown, I'll show 'em to you. You had the Economy Hall. You had the...
...Cooperators Hall. On Ursuline and Drury. Two blocks away was the Cooperators Hall.

On Liberty and Marais. Two blocks from that, at Lafitte and Orleans, was the Globe Hall, which ceased to be a hall, and became a gambling house. Then you had the First Veterans Hall. Then you had... All these halls were about four blocks from one another. I'll show you where they were. And then there was the clubs. The San Jacinto Club right in the midst of that, a great big club. And two blocks away was the Lions Club. See? All that's in about...

In six or eight blocks there's all these halls. You see. And a certain number of people went to them halls. The people at the Lions wouldn't go to the First Veterans Hall because they was different color strata. For every color of the rainbow, you had a hall.

Yeah. Everybody had their hall. Similar to New York, you'd see the speakeasy, where they'd peep through the hole, and they would say, 'Well, yeah, we'll let you in.' Well, they had that down in New Orleans. Because if you knocked on the door, they had a hole to look through to

see if you're the (?) color or if anybody know you. They say, "Okay, wait until (?) gets up. Do you know who that is out there? There's somebody out there wanting to come in." They were very careful(?) and particular who they associated with. So if you had a stigma of being anything that's unnatural or being any kind of character, certain people would have nothing to do with you. That was your backside. None of them would associate with you. You were relegated to get on the outskirts and get out. Don't be coming here. Because you're not invited. They'd let you know.
